page_hero.title: Legacy System Modernization Services
page_hero.subtitle: Transform aging COBOL, ASP.NET, Java EE, and VB.NET systems into modern cloud-native platforms—without freezing your roadmap or losing decades of business logic.

why_modernize.intro: Every day you keep a legacy system running is a day you pay in three currencies: ballooning maintenance costs, lost competitive agility, and mounting security risk. Modernization is not a sunk cost—it is a high-leverage investment that pays back within 18–24 months for most B2B organizations.
paragraphs: Most enterprises underestimate how much legacy debt compounds. A 2019 Deloitte study found that 60% of CIOs say their technical debt actively blocks new product launches, and the average Fortune 1000 firm spends more than 70% of its IT budget just keeping the lights on. That is a destructive ratio: every dollar spent on legacy maintenance is a dollar not invested in AI, customer experience, or new revenue lines. Legacy system modernization flips that ratio, freeing capital and talent for work that actually moves the business forward.

Security is the second urgent driver. Legacy stacks like Windows Server 2008, Java 6, PHP 5.x, and classic ASP no longer receive vendor patches, yet they routinely hold mission-critical data—customer records, payment flows, manufacturing telemetry. Attackers specifically target these unpatched stacks because exploits are well-documented and defenses are thin. Migrating to a modern, supported platform like .NET 8, Spring Boot 3, or a managed Kubernetes service on Azure or AWS collapses your attack surface, keeps you compliant with PCI DSS, HIPAA, and GDPR, and gives auditors a defensible posture.

The third pressure is talent. The median COBOL developer in 2024 is 55 years old and retiring faster than replacements are trained. ASP.NET Web Forms, classic VB6, and Oracle Forms developers are following the same curve. Each retirement is not a routine handoff; it is institutional knowledge walking out the door—the comment blocks, the tribal workarounds, the unwritten invariants that keep the system alive. A structured modernization effort captures that knowledge while it still exists, translates it into modern code, and lets the next generation of engineers actually understand the platform they inherit.

Finally, modernization unlocks the AI and automation capabilities your competitors are already deploying. You cannot bolt a modern LLM-powered workflow onto a 1990s mainframe—the integration surface is too narrow, the data model is too rigid, and the release cycle is too slow. A modernized platform gives you real-time APIs, event streams, vector databases, and containerized workloads that make AI integration a 6-week project instead of a 3-year re-platforming exercise. The question is no longer whether to modernize but how to do it without taking the business offline.

process.title: Our Modernization Approach
process.subtitle: A six-phase methodology engineered to deliver value early, de-risk the migration, and keep your business running throughout.

steps.title: Discovery & Technical Debt Audit
steps.text: We map every dependency, integration, and business rule in your current system. You receive a quantified technical debt report, a risk heat map, and a list of quick wins that can ship in 30 days.

steps.title: Modernization Strategy & Roadmap
steps.text: We design a phased delivery plan that aligns with your business priorities—re-platform, refactor, rehost, or replace per domain. You get a fixed-price proposal, milestone schedule, and rollback strategy.

steps.title: Architecture & Reference Implementation
steps.text: We build a vertical-slice reference implementation that proves out the target stack, deployment pipeline, and observability stack. You see real production-shaped code before we commit to full delivery.

steps.title: Iterative Migration & Parallel Run
steps.text: Domain by domain, we ship new code while the legacy system keeps running. We run both systems in parallel, reconcile outputs daily, and only cut traffic once parity is provably achieved.

steps.title: Cutover, Hardening & Hyper-Care
steps.text: Zero-downtime cutover using feature flags, blue/green deployments, and shadow traffic. We provide 30 days of hyper-care: 24/7 on-call, war-room coverage, and rapid rollback paths.

steps.title: Optimization & Continuous Modernization
steps.text: After launch, we instrument every workload, tune performance, and feed a backlog of continuous modernization opportunities—keeping the system modern for the next decade, not just the next release.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about legacy system modernization with Barbuk.

items.question: How long does a typical legacy system modernization project take?
items.answer: Most ASP.NET modernization projects run 3 to 6 months. Full enterprise re-platformings—migrating COBOL, Java EE, or large .NET Framework estates—typically take 9 to 18 months. We always deliver in phases, so you start seeing business value within the first 6 to 8 weeks. The first vertical slice proves the architecture; subsequent domains are faster because the pattern is already established.

items.question: What is the strangler-fig pattern and why do you recommend it?
items.answer: The strangler-fig pattern is a migration strategy where you incrementally replace pieces of a legacy system with new services while the original system continues to run. A routing layer gradually shifts traffic from old to new until the legacy system is fully retired. We recommend it because it eliminates big-bang cutover risk, lets you validate parity in production with real users, and allows rollback at any phase. It is the only pattern we have seen deliver zero customer-facing downtime on a 1M+ line codebase.

items.question: Can you modernize our COBOL or mainframe system without losing business logic?
items.answer: Yes. We use a three-layer approach. First, AI-assisted code translation converts the syntactic structure of COBOL, JCL, and copybooks to Java or C#. Second, our domain experts—former mainframe developers—manually review every business rule, validation, and edge case to make sure the logic is faithfully represented. Third, we run both systems in parallel for a full reconciliation period, comparing outputs row-by-row before any traffic is cut. The end result is a system that behaves identically to the original, with the maintainability of a modern codebase.

items.question: Do we need to pause business operations during the migration?
items.answer: No. Our zero-downtime methodology is designed exactly for that. We use dual-write database windows, shadow traffic, feature flags, and blue/green deployments to ensure the legacy system continues serving customers throughout the migration. The only times we ask for short maintenance windows (typically 15 to 60 minutes) are for final DNS or load-balancer cutovers, and we schedule them for your lowest-traffic periods. For the case study above, we completed a 14-month migration of a core banking platform with zero minutes of customer-facing downtime.

items.question: What does legacy system modernization cost, and how do you price it?
items.answer: Pricing depends on the size and complexity of your system, the target architecture, and the migration strategy. As a rough guide, ASP.NET to .NET 8 modernization projects start around $45,000 and scale based on codebase size. Full enterprise re-platformings typically range from $250,000 to $1.5M+. We always work from a fixed-price proposal after a paid discovery sprint, so there are no hourly billing surprises. Most clients see positive ROI within 18 months through reduced licensing, lower maintenance overhead, and faster time-to-market for new features.
